question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Fish out of water

options.text: Not feeling comfortable in a new environment

solution:
The correct answer is **"Not feeling comfortable in a new environment."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom** "fish out of water"** means to feel uncomfortable or out of place in a new environment or situation. (किसी नए वातावरण या स्थिति में असहज या जगह से बाहर महसूस करना)

 
 
• **Example**:* After moving to a new city, I felt like a **fish out of water**__ until I made some friends and got used to the area.*
 
 
 
• The phrase is often used to describe someone who is struggling to adapt to a new job, school, or social setting.
 
• The idiom comes from the idea that a fish removed from water will struggle to survive, just as a person removed from their familiar surroundings may feel lost or disoriented.
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.
